title: Luttons, UK - a ticking pocket watch ...
author: david m
notes: A wind-up skeleton pocket watch ticking, recorded through contact mics on the watch (Olympus LS-14), so it is about as close and small as a tick can be: a crisp, silvery ~6 ticks/s escapement, LRA 1 dB over the segment, nothing else in it. Energy is 2-16 kHz once the hp removes the contact-mic rumble and a faint 750 Hz recorder tone (both well under the ticks; hp 1200 is part of the pick). The two

title: clockmaker, gosposka ulica 26, maribor - chronos synchronicity
author: OR poiesis
notes: Inside a clock-repair workshop (clock master Jože Vidovič, Gosposka ulica 26, Maribor): many small old clocks ticking at different rates, a dense, even, wide-stereo patter (L/R corr ~0 after hp), LRA 1.2 dB, no strikes, no chimes, no voices in this take (the sister takes 26044/25970 have strikes and were not used). Caveat: the raw file carries a strong sub-150 Hz rumble (93% of its energy below 60

title: Unnamed Road, Malton YO17 8TJ, UK - windup clockwork christmas gonks ...
author: david m
notes: Winding a little clockwork toy by its key: four slow ratchet strokes (a fine click-train in 2-16 kHz) and a last few clicks, then stops before the toy is released at 8.95 s. DPA 4060s into a Zoom H5, very close. Reads as a small clock or music-box being wound. hp removes a low room rumble/hum below ~900 Hz.

title: Unnamed Road, Malton YO17 8TJ, UK - windup clockwork xmas gonks ...
author: david m
notes: A second winding take (another toy from the same set): five ratchet strokes of different lengths with soft clicks between, close and dry; ends before the toy starts at 12.4 s.

title: Unnamed Road, Malton YO17 8TJ, UK - windup clockwork xmas gonks ...
author: david m
notes: A wind-up clockwork toy's spring mechanism running down: ~5.5 s of busy, fine gear whirr (2-16 kHz) that stops dead at 45.9 s when the spring is spent, with its room tail. Starts mid-run, so it needs the fade-in. These are small festive 'gonk' toys, so some of the texture is their feet pattering on the table; no music, no squeak.

title: bonifazius, bürknerstr. - mechanical toy
author: udo noll
notes: A hand-driven mechanical toy with a centrifugal flywheel: one crank spins it up to a humming whirr (~100-200 Hz fundamental with a fine metallic chatter above) and it then spins down on its own over ~5 s to silence at ~27.5 s, like a governor or top running down. Natural decay kept. Low-heavy: do not hp above ~50 Hz.

title: Poznan, Mateckiego Street, bathroom - steam cleaner
author: maciej janasik
notes: Steam escaping from the valve of a household steam cleaner as it is closed: a soft, smooth hiss (mostly 1.5-6 kHz) that eases off by ~10 dB over 6 s. Used as the little puff of steam from an instrument. The hiss was already running, so the fade-in makes the 'puff' onset; the cut ends just before the valve thread squeaks at 108.8 s.

title: Różana 4, 58-351 Różana, Poland - snoring gently
author: zvukac
notes: Sleeper A (in a tent, Poland; 'snoring gently'): two slow, soft inhale-snores (~2.7 s each, 50-600 Hz with a 1-1.4 kHz nasal formant) and the quiet between them. Peaceful and regular, no rasp, no words, no rustle. +25 dB over the floor in band. The lp removes faint dawn birds at 4-8 kHz.

title: Różana 4, 58-351 Różana, Poland - snoring gently
author: zvukac
notes: Sleeper A, an earlier, slightly more tonal pair: each snore has a gently gliding 100-150 Hz tone in it (a soft 'whistly' purr), two breaths. A faint bird at 3.1 kHz elsewhere is removed by the lp.

title: Ulupınar Mahallesi, Çıralı Yolu, 07980 Kemer/Antalya, Turkey - Snoring
author: akile nazli kaya
notes: Sleeper B (camp at night, Antalya, Turkey; FLAC): two breath cycles, each a breathy inhale-snore then a soft exhale, and each with a tiny tonal whistle (~650-700 Hz) at the top of the snore: the 'deep sleeping breath with a little whistle'. Airier than A (energy up to ~12 kHz). +29 dB over the floor; hp clears a low noise floor.

title: Ulupınar Mahallesi, Çıralı Yolu, 07980 Kemer/Antalya, Turkey - Snoring
author: akile nazli kaya
notes: Sleeper B, a fuller snore with a buzzy 130-200 Hz rattle-tone (the most 'comic' of the set) followed by a shorter, quieter one. Not harsh, but the loudest of B's breaths; keep its level modest.

title: Snoring Person Recording D. D. Teoli Jr.
author: D. D. Teoli Jr.
notes: Sleeper C (D. D. Teoli Jr., public domain): two short, soft snores ~3.8 s apart (100-1000 Hz with breathy air above), +24 dB over the floor. A plain, undramatic sleeping snore. The source is a modest-quality MP3 with a low broadband floor; hp 150 cleans it.

title: Pedernales Falls State Park, TX, USA - Friend Snoring in Tent after Vino
author: Sylvia Shale
notes: Sleeper D (a friend asleep in a tent, Pedernales Falls, Texas; DPA 4060s): two short, deep, throaty snores (40-600 Hz) with a little 500-600 Hz exhale tone after each. The deepest voice of the set. A katydid tone at 2.3 kHz runs under the whole recording, so the lp 1800 is required; source is lossy (cut at ~10 kHz).

title: XC1015003 Hermit Thrush (Catharus guttatus)
author: Stanislas Wroza
notes: Hermit thrush (Catharus guttatus), xeno-canto quality A, recordist already high-passed below ~1.7 kHz. Six song phrases at ~4.5 s spacing (1.4, 5.7, 10.5, 14.5, 18.3, 22.9 s) with clean silences and the last phrase's tail. In-band SNR ~69 dB, floor -76 dBFS: near-anechoic, very close and dry. Bécancour, Québec. 48 kHz 16-bit WAV original (stereo, LR corr 0.66; downmix is fine). Ends before a buzzy

title: XC1015003 Hermit Thrush (Catharus guttatus)
author: Stanislas Wroza
notes: Hermit thrush (Catharus guttatus), xeno-canto quality A, recordist already high-passed below ~1.7 kHz. Same bird as phoenix-1, six different phrases (31.7, 35.9, 40.3, 45.0, 48.9, 53.4 s) with natural gaps. SNR ~69 dB, nothing else audible. 48 kHz WAV original.

title: XC1015003 Hermit Thrush (Catharus guttatus)
author: Stanislas Wroza
notes: Hermit thrush (Catharus guttatus), xeno-canto quality A, recordist already high-passed below ~1.7 kHz. Same bird, seven phrases (80.1 to 108.0 s) including the high-pitched variants. SNR ~60 dB. Ends at 110.5 s, just before another buzzy trill at 110.8 s. 48 kHz WAV original.

title: XC601488 Hermit Thrush (Catharus guttatus)
author: Christopher McPherson
notes: Hermit thrush (Catharus guttatus), xeno-canto quality A, recordist already high-passed below ~1.7 kHz. A second bird (New Hampshire): five loud close phrases (3.0, 8.0, 13.1, 18.2, 21.9 s), SNR ~60 dB. Between phrases a faint distant chorus (other thrushes/small birds) sits 35-45 dB below the song, effectively inaudible once played quietly with reverb. 48 kHz 320 kbps MP3, mono.

title: XC601488 Hermit Thrush (Catharus guttatus)
author: Christopher McPherson
notes: Hermit thrush (Catharus guttatus), xeno-canto quality A, recordist already high-passed below ~1.7 kHz. Same NH bird, five more phrases (59.7, 64.7, 69.3, 76.5, 81.0 s) with the longer 7 s pause in the middle. SNR ~61 dB; same faint background chorus 35-45 dB down. 48 kHz 320 kbps MP3, mono.

title: XC691469 Hermit Thrush (Catharus guttatus)
author: Christopher McPherson
notes: Hermit thrush (Catharus guttatus), xeno-canto quality A, recordist already high-passed below ~1.7 kHz. A third bird (Hollis, NH): six phrases (60.5, 65.0, 69.8, 74.6, 80.3, 87.0 s). SNR ~45 dB with hp 2500; there is a broadband low-mid noise floor (distant road/wind) below ~3 kHz that hp 2500 removes, plus faint insect-like bands at 3.7/4.4 kHz ~40 dB down. Least clean of the six; 44.1 kHz 128 kbp

title: GOLD TAPE: 21 Birds - G21-05 Wing Flutter
author: USC Cinema / Sunset Editorial sound effects collection
notes: Old USC/Sunset Editorial SFX library (mono, tape-era: content rolls off above ~6-7 kHz, so it is soft and warm rather than crisp). A bird ruffling/fluttering its feathers: soft rustle with fine feather ticks swelling to a quick flutter at 7.2 s and dying away. Very quiet room, floor -64 dBFS, in-band SNR ~34 dB. No calls.

title: GOLD TAPE: 21 Birds - G21-05 Wing Flutter
author: USC Cinema / Sunset Editorial sound effects collection
notes: Old USC/Sunset Editorial SFX library (mono, tape-era: content rolls off above ~6-7 kHz, so it is soft and warm rather than crisp). The end of a long flutter: a bird settling, with soft, fading feather rustles over 5 s. Starts mid-rustle (about -43 dBFS, needs the usual short fade-in), SNR ~25 dB. No calls.

title: Red Library: Animals Birds - R21-40b Bird Wings Flapping
author: USC Cinema / Sunset Editorial sound effects collection
notes: Old USC/Sunset Editorial SFX library (mono, tape-era: content rolls off above ~6-7 kHz, so it is soft and warm rather than crisp). A short bout of wing flapping (about 7 beats, 18.4-19.5 s) then the feathers settling, decaying into silence by 20.4 s. SNR ~24 dB. No calls (no harmonic content on a linear 0-3 kHz view). The bird species is not stated. A faint steady ~270 Hz tape tone sits ~40 dB und

title: Kolonia Mazurska, Mierki, Poland - (853 AB) Fireplace in the woods
author: Piotrek Zyla
notes: Big wood fire recorded close with a pair of Sennheiser MKH 8020 omnis (AB, 17 cm) into a Sound Devices MixPre-6 II, as lossless 48 kHz FLAC. A deep, steady roar (most of the energy is at 60-250 Hz, and the low end is fully correlated L/R, so it is the fire, not wind) with a dense spray of crackles and the odd soft hiss of sap.
